 Maatrubhumi song ‘Madirapan’: Salman Khan takes a break from war to enjoy a drink. Watch 
 Maatrubhumi song 'Madirapan', composed by Himesh Reshamiya, shows Salman Khan and his fellow Indian Army men put their war worries at bay for a celebration. 
 By: Entertainment Desk 3 min read Mumbai Nov 19, 2026 08:08 PM IST 
 Maatrubhumi song "Madirapan": Salman Khan takes a break from war to drink. Photo Courtesy: YouTube screengrab.

 Salman Khan Films has dropped another song ahead of the long-awaited release of Salman Khan’s military drama Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace. The dance number, “Madirapan”, sees Salman and his fellow Indian Army men take a break from war to enjoy some revelry.
 What’s in the new Maatrubhumi song?
 “Madirapan” starts with Salman Khan’s character declaring, “ Jashn ho jaye ” (Let’s celebrate). On his orders, mugs are filled, empty glass bottles are smashed on the ground, and spare alcohol is used to fuel the bonfire. As his battalion kicks off the celebration, a solemn-looking Salman orders, “Saavdhan!” (Attention!).
 When the room stands still, Salman follows it up with another command, “ Vishram !” (Stand at ease!), and then breaks into a dance. He then begins to remove his cap, sunglasses, and jacket before grabbing the spotlight and shaking a leg as his fellow men surround him and cheer. As the battalion put the worries of war at bay for the moment and steal a night of revelry, they soon sense something is missing.

 Since they’re all away from home, their wives show up to join the celebration. Of course, they’re not actually present there, but only manifest themselves because the soldiers are missing them. Chitrangda Singh, who plays Salman’s wife, even pops up dressed in the military uniform, wearing a military cap and dark sunglasses, and flexing her biceps like her husband.
 As Salman shakes his head in disbelief, Chitrangda swiftly switches to a colourful salwar suit before shaking a leg with him. Salman joins in, wrapping her translucent orange dupatta around his neck as they get intimate. The ladies soon bid goodbye and disappear, as the men continue to dance and party the night away.
 More on Maatrubhumi
 “Madirapan”, the sixth song released from Maatrubhumi’s album, is also composed by Himesh Reshammiya, who’s had a stellar track record with Salman Khan, with hits like Sohail Khan’s 1998 romantic comedy Pyaar Kiya To Darna Kya, Satish Kaushik’s 2003 romantic film Tere Naam, the title track of Siddique’s Bodyguard (2011), and Sooraj Barjatya’s Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (2015).
 “Madirapan” is sung by Javed Ali, Mohd Danish, and Soumee Sailesh, written by Sameer Anjjan, and choreographed by Mudassar Khan. Salman Khan Films Music has already dropped five songs from the film — Arijit Singh and Shreya Ghoshal’s title track, “Main Hoon”, “Chand Dekh Lena”, “Jai Hind”, and “Teri Sexy Beauty”, sung by Salman himself.

 After several hurdles, Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace has been cleared with the Central Board of Film Certification granting a ‘U/A’ certificate. It was initially titled Battle of Galwan, but the title was changed after reported objection from the Information & Broadcasting Ministry. The movie is  slated to release in cinemas on December 4.
